blocks.text: The fundamental particles are considered to be the six quarks, the six leptons and the gauge bosons (and the Higgs boson); the gauge bosons are the carriers of the fundamental forces. Leptons and quarks interact with each other by sending and receiving bosons. For example, electromagnetic interactions occur when two charged particles send and receive (exchange) photons; the photons are said to carry the force between charged particles. Likewise, attraction between two quarks in an atomic nucleus occurs when the quarks send and receive gluons. Similarly the W+, W- and Z bosons are the carriers of the weak nuclear force, and gravitons are the proposed carriers of the gravitational force.

blocks.title: Higgs boson
blocks.text: The Higgs boson is a special particle discovered in 2012 at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. It is associated with the Higgs field, which permeates all of space. Its crucial role is that it explains how other particles get mass by interacting with the field.

Particles that interact strongly with the Higgs field get more mass, such as the carriers of the electroweak interaction, the W+, W- and Z bosons, whereas particles like photons do not interact with the Higgs field, so their rest mass is zero. The Higgs boson has a mass of about 125 giga-electron-volts (GeV) and decays rapidly into other particles. Key facts:

items: The Higgs boson gets its mass from its interactions with its associated Higgs field.
It can be a unique window on the conditions of the universe shortly after the Big Bang and on signs of dark matter, because of its distinctive properties.
